andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh steps up disaster preparedness as Bay of Bengal low-pressure system approaches the coast
facts: On 21 September, the IMD forecast heavy rain in isolated parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema, with thunderstorms and lightning.
The system was forecast to move towards the north Andhra Pradesh–south Odisha coast around 23 September; it remained a forecast, not an observed landfall.
Andhra Pradesh officials were directed to keep control rooms operational 24 hours and maintain readiness for possible evacuations from vulnerable coastal and low-lying areas.
The State was advised to keep SDRF and NDRF teams ready and coordinate with districts bordering Odisha.
Coastal wind speeds of around 50–60 kmph were cited in the preparedness guidance.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: The 20 September briefing covered the Bay of Bengal low-pressure system and its projected approach towards the Andhra coast. Today: Andhra Pradesh authorities stepped up response preparations, including round-the-clock control rooms, response-team readiness and precautionary evacuation planning; the system’s intensification and coastal approach remained forecasts.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Disaster management cycle: early warning, preparedness, inter-district coordination and evacuation planning for cyclones and floods.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish a low-pressure system or forecast depression from a cyclone and from an observed landfall; note the role of IMD warnings and SDRF/NDRF preparedness.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how forecast-based action, inter-state coordination and last-mile warnings can reduce loss of life and property in coastal and flood-prone districts.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: the forecast and preparedness measures concern Andhra Pradesh’s coastal and other districts, with coordination advised for districts bordering Odisha.

national.headline: India–New Zealand FTA set to enter into force on 20 October 2026
facts: India and New Zealand announced that their Free Trade Agreement will enter into force on 20 October 2026.
The agreement was signed in New Delhi on 27 April 2026; New Zealand’s Parliament passed its implementing legislation on 16 September 2026.
India’s exports to New Zealand are to receive zero-duty access from the agreement’s first day, according to the Commerce Ministry.
The announcement followed completion of internal processes in both countries; the FTA was not yet in force on 21 September.
national.summary: India and New Zealand announced the FTA’s implementation date after completing their internal processes. The agreement is scheduled to take effect on 20 October 2026, so the announcement should not be treated as the start of tariff preferences on 21 September.
national.staticLink: Free trade agreements; trade liberalisation; bilateral economic diplomacy.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the scheduled effective date: 20 October 2026; distinguish the 21 September announcement from the agreement’s entry into force.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how FTAs can expand export access and investment while requiring domestic adjustment and implementation capacity.

national.headline: Supreme Court clarifies when court deposits stop post-award interest; refers uniform rules to Law Commission
facts: In National Seeds Corporation Ltd. v. National Agro Seed Corporation (India), the Supreme Court considered deposits made while enforcement of an arbitral award was stayed.
The Court held that a deposit does not by itself count as payment if the award-holder cannot access it unconditionally; interest may continue in that situation.
The judgment applied Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, and Order XXI Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

The Court asked the Law Commission of India to examine the need for suitable legislation on the handling, investment and release of court and tribunal deposits, in consultation with the RBI and Union ministries.
national.summary: A Supreme Court bench of Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe ruled on the effect of a court deposit on interest owed under an arbitral award. It also referred the broader issue of non-uniform court-deposit practices to the Law Commission for examination; this is a referral, not enacted legislation.
national.staticLink: Enforcement of arbitral awards; civil procedure; separation of adjudication and law reform.
national.prelimsTakeaway: A conditional deposit unavailable for unconditional withdrawal is not necessarily payment that stops interest under Order XXI Rule 1 CPC.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how consistent rules for court-held funds can promote equal treatment of litigants and reduce disputes over interest and investment.

national.headline: India launches the 7th National Formulary and new medicine- and device-safety measures
facts: Union Minister of State for Health Anupriya Patel launched the 7th edition of the National Formulary of India (NFI), also made available online.
The NFI is a prescribing guidance resource intended to support appropriate and rational use of medicines.
The launch also included the ADR-PvPI 2.0 mobile app for iOS users and hospital guidance on reporting adverse events related to medical devices.

The Government approved the Biovigilance Programme of India; the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission is to lead monitoring of adverse events associated with products used in organ and tissue transplantation.
The Ministry reported around 1,150 adverse drug reaction reporting centres operating nationwide.
national.summary: At the 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week, the Health Ministry launched an updated prescribing reference and additional reporting and monitoring tools. Separately, it announced government approval of a biovigilance programme covering adverse events linked to transplant-related medicines and biological products.
national.staticLink: Pharmacovigilance; rational use of medicines; patient safety and public-health regulation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: NFI supports rational prescribing; PvPI tracks adverse drug reactions; the new Biovigilance Programme addresses safety monitoring in organ and tissue transplantation.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how pharmacovigilance, materiovigilance and biovigilance can strengthen patient safety, and the challenges of reporting adverse events across health facilities.

national.headline: Defence Ministry signs ₹586-crore contract for indigenous tank auxiliary power units
facts: The Ministry of Defence signed a ₹586-crore contract with Accurate Industrial Controls Private Limited for Auxiliary Power Units (APUs) for T-72 and T-90 tanks.
The contract was signed in New Delhi on 21 September 2026.
The APUs provide an alternative source of electrical power for tank systems including fire control, firing circuits and gun stabilisation.
The Ministry described the APUs as indigenously developed and linked the procurement to industry-led Make-II research and development.
national.summary: The Defence Ministry contracted for indigenous APUs intended to support the operational readiness and reliability of T-72 and T-90 tank formations. The announcement concerns a procurement contract; it does not mean the equipment has already been delivered or inducted.
national.staticLink: Defence indigenisation; Make-II procurement; military technology and operational readiness.
national.prelimsTakeaway: An auxiliary power unit supplies electrical power to tank systems; the contract covers T-72 and T-90 platforms.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how domestic development and procurement of critical subsystems can strengthen defence preparedness and reduce import dependence.

national.headline: 18th India–Mongolia exercise Nomadic Elephant begins in Pithoragarh
facts: The 18th edition of the annual India–Mongolia joint military exercise Nomadic Elephant commenced at the Foreign Training Node, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand.
The exercise is scheduled from 21 September to 3 October 2026 and is conducted alternately in India and Mongolia.
The Indian Army and Mongolian Armed Forces are each represented by 45 personnel.

Training includes counter-insurgency operations in semi-urban and mountainous terrain under a UN mandate, with drills involving drones, counter-drone systems, cyber security and special heliborne operations.
national.summary: India and Mongolia began the 18th edition of their platoon-level joint exercise in Uttarakhand. The programme is scheduled to continue through 3 October and focuses on tactical interoperability and counter-insurgency operations in challenging terrain.
national.staticLink: India’s bilateral defence cooperation; military exercises; UN peacekeeping and interoperability.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Nomadic Elephant is an annual India–Mongolia platoon-level exercise; the 2026 edition is at Pithoragarh.
national.mainsAngle: Explain how joint exercises build interoperability and deepen defence ties while improving preparedness for multinational and terrain-specific operations.

national.headline: India wins men’s 10m air-rifle team silver at Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games
facts: India’s team of Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, Himanshu Dhillon and Parth Rakesh Mane won silver in the men’s 10m air-rifle team event.
The Indian team scored 1,890.1; China won gold with 1,899.0, a world-record score, and the Republic of Korea took bronze with 1,884.2.
The event was held at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi–Nagoya, Japan; the ISSF records the team event on 21 September 2026.
India also secured silver and bronze in the men’s individual event through Himanshu Dhillon and Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil, respectively.
national.summary: Previous: the Aichi–Nagoya Asian Games opening was covered. Today: India earned a men’s 10m air-rifle team silver, while China set a world record for gold; Indian shooters also took silver and bronze in the individual final.
national.staticLink: Asian Games; international multi-sport events; shooting disciplines and medal results.

national.headline: I-STEM brings state nodal officers together to widen access to public research infrastructure
facts: The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser convened its first State Governments Nodal Officers Meeting for the I-STEM portal on 21 September.
The meeting involved nodal officers from 23 States and 4 Union Territories and discussed linking state universities, laboratories and research facilities to the national platform.
The government reported that I-STEM listed more than 31,000 scientific instruments across nearly 4,000 institutions and had over 65,000 registered users.
The stated aims include improving shared access to publicly funded equipment, increasing utilisation and reducing duplication of research-infrastructure investment.
national.summary: The meeting focused on state-level coordination and onboarding institutions to I-STEM, an existing national platform for discovering and accessing scientific facilities. It was a coordination step, not the launch of a new portal or a guarantee that every state institution is already onboarded.
national.staticLink: Public research infrastructure; science and technology governance; digital platforms for innovation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: I-STEM connects researchers and institutions with publicly funded scientific equipment and facilities.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how shared access to research infrastructure can reduce duplication and improve innovation, while identifying the need for equitable access and effective state-level coordination.

national.headline: CSIR road-research institute to support safer-road planning in Visakhapatnam
facts: CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI) met with Visakhapatnam Metropolitan Region Development Authority (VMRDA) and Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) to plan scientific road-improvement support.
The city programme described in the release covers about 228 km of roads, 34 km of central medians and more than 1,550 street lights across eight constituencies.
CSIR-CRRI surveyed selected road stretches and assessed road condition, geometric design, safety, signs, junctions and pedestrian facilities.

Proposed areas for technical work include road-safety audits, urban flooding and coastal-erosion studies, pavement improvements and a Road Asset Management System; proposed MoAs/MoUs were still to be finalised.
national.summary: CSIR-CRRI began technical engagement with VMRDA and GVMC and surveyed selected stretches in Visakhapatnam. The parties discussed proposed agreements and possible studies; these agreements and recommendations should not be treated as completed works.
national.staticLink: Urban transport and road safety; resilient infrastructure; coastal and urban disaster-risk reduction.
national.prelimsTakeaway: CSIR-CRRI is the Central Road Research Institute under CSIR; the Visakhapatnam engagement involves VMRDA and GVMC.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how scientific road audits, resilient pavement design and coordinated urban planning can improve safety and reduce climate-related infrastructure risks in coastal cities.
national.apLink: The development directly concerns Visakhapatnam: CSIR-CRRI is working with VMRDA and GVMC on road surveys and technical planning.

international.headline: India joins Partners for Multilateralism summit declaration on international cooperation
facts: The Partners for Multilateralism (P4M) summit was convened on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly High-Level Week.
India was among the initial co-sponsors, alongside Australia, Barbados, Brazil, Canada, the EU and Kenya.
The declaration reaffirmed the UN Charter, international law, peaceful settlement of disputes and the need to reform multilateral institutions.
It called for cooperation on resilient supply chains, trade, international finance, AI, climate change and global health.
international.summary: The P4M summit issued a joint declaration on 21 September 2026, with India among its initial co-sponsors. It commits participants to cooperation and multilateral reform; it is a political declaration, not a treaty creating binding obligations.
international.staticLink: United Nations system; multilateralism; international law and India’s foreign policy.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember P4M’s full name, the 21 September 2026 summit date, India’s role as an initial co-sponsor and the declaration’s emphasis on UN reform and international law.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how India can use issue-based, cross-regional coalitions to support a more representative multilateral order while advancing practical cooperation.

international.headline: Planetary Health Check 2026 reports seven of nine planetary boundaries breached
facts: The Planetary Health Check 2026 was released on 21 September by Planetary Boundaries Science at the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research.
It assesses nine planetary boundaries; seven are transgressed, and the report says all seven are at their highest recorded levels of transgression.
The seven include climate change, biosphere integrity, land-system change, freshwater change, biogeochemical flows, novel entities and ocean acidification.
The report says the stratospheric ozone and atmospheric aerosol-loading boundaries have shown improvement over the last decade, while noting unsafe aerosol levels remain in some regions.
international.summary: The 2026 Planetary Health Check was published on 21 September, reporting worsening pressure across Earth’s life-support systems. It identifies ocean acidification as the latest boundary to have crossed its threshold, in 2025; the assessment is a scientific report, not an intergovernmental treaty or index ranking.
international.staticLink: Earth-system science; planetary boundaries; climate change, biodiversity and sustainable development.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Recall the nine-boundary framework, the finding that seven are transgressed, and that ocean acidification was the latest boundary to cross its threshold in 2025.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the value and limits of planetary-boundary assessments for integrated environmental governance and climate-policy choices.

international.headline: Accra Reset panel releases proposals to reform global health governance
facts: Ghana’s President John Dramani Mahama presented the Accra Reset High-Level Panel report, A Sovereign Future for Health, at a 21 September 2026 UNGA-week event in New York.
The report sets out five proposed political shifts and ten recommendations for global health architecture and governance.
Recommendations include country-led health compacts, stronger regional functions, coordinated procurement and regional health manufacturing.
The panel proposes independent follow-up within six months and country-led compacts within twelve months; these are proposed timelines, not completed reforms.
international.summary: The report frames health sovereignty as strengthening country-defined priorities and national and regional capabilities within global cooperation. Its recommendations and implementation horizons are proposals; the report does not record reforms already carried out.
international.staticLink: Global health governance; international organisations; public health systems and health equity.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Know the report title, its five political shifts and ten recommendations, and distinguish its proposed follow-up timelines from completed action.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how country ownership, regional cooperation and global public goods can be balanced in reforming international health governance.

international.headline: International Day of Peace 2026 highlights everyday peacebuilding
facts: The United Nations observed the International Day of Peace on 21 September 2026 under the theme “Invest in Peace: For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day”.
The UN observance highlighted local and everyday peacebuilders, including people advancing dialogue and community stability.
The UN General Assembly established the day in 1981; in 2001 it designated it as a period of non-violence and cease-fire.
international.summary: The 2026 observance focused on investment in peace through everyday action, dialogue and community-level peacebuilding. The date is observed annually on 21 September.
international.staticLink: United Nations and international observances; culture of peace; conflict prevention and peacekeeping.
international.prelimsTakeaway: International Day of Peace: 21 September; 2026 theme: “Invest in Peace: For Everyone, Everywhere, Every Day”; established by the UN General Assembly in 1981.
international.mainsAngle: Explain how inclusive local peacebuilding and investment in human development can complement diplomacy and formal peace processes.
